purpose: Test a pollination-independent sufficient-condition account of determinant-rank crossover before admitting any generic numerical result to the manuscript.

theory_targets.smooth_response_asymptotic: For Y_k=f(X,Zbar_k), with iid finite-variance community draws and f smooth near the mean community state, the starting-state main effect tends to a nonzero O(1) limit when Var_X[f(X,mu)]>0, whereas the community main effect is O(1/k). The state-by-community interaction is also O(1/k) to first order and may remain substantial at finite k.
theory_targets.exact_bilinear_special_case: For centered independent X and Zbar_k and f(x,z)=a*x+b*z+c*x*z, S_k=a^2 Var(X), C_k=b^2 Var(Zbar_k), I_k=c^2 Var(X) Var(Zbar_k).
theory_targets.correlated_countercondition: For exchangeable community copies with pairwise correlation rho, Var(Zbar_k)=sigma^2[rho+(1-rho)/k], creating a stochasticity floor. Rank crossover is not guaranteed when the asymptotic community floor is at least the starting-state component.

predeclared_checks: For rho=0, community main effect decreases exactly as 1/k while starting-state main effect is constant.
For rho=0, starting-state main effect is smaller than community at k=1 and larger by sufficiently large k.
For rho=0, interaction remains positive at every finite k when c is nonzero.
For rho=0.4 with the frozen coefficients, the community variance floor exceeds the starting-state component, so no asymptotic rank crossover is predicted.
The generic audit must not use any Chapter 2 pollinator parameter, seed, trajectory, richness value or response matrix.
claim_boundary: This generalization supplies sufficient conditions, not necessary conditions, for determinant-rank crossover.
The model-specific crossover near k=4 remains an internal numerical result and is not promoted to a natural threshold.
Finite-k interaction persistence does not imply that interaction remains nonzero in the independent-copy k-to-infinity limit.
Correlated or synchronously forced community realizations can prevent stochastic averaging and therefore prevent rank crossover.
